role: The legislative decree makes it a national market-surveillance authority under the AI Regulation, limited to what Article 74(8) of that regulation provides.

name: NASK AI Safety Research Centre
role: The Ministry of Digital Affairs says the new centre's researchers "focus on innovative AI research, with an emphasis on cybersecurity". NASK's director describes "the cooperation between the Korea AI Safety Institute at ETRI and the AI Safety Research Center at NASK". On NASK's research teams page, the centre's Department of Security and Transparency of Artificial Intelligence says "We develop methods for generating, analyzing and auditing models, and develop methods and software to support their analysis". The Ministry of Digital Affairs quotes the centre's director: the centre "is also tasked with educating and supporting society in the informed use of modern AI technologies". NASK says the centre will lead its cooperation with OpenAI and "will research the safety of increasingly advanced AI systems" with it.

name: Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment
RTR KI-Servicestelle

The government's report says the Office for Digital Innovation is currently designing the AI regulatory sandbox that Article 57 of the AI Act requires.

Luxembourg AI Factory
role: The Ministry of the Economy says the Luxembourg AI Factory is the national platform dedicated to the responsible and secure adoption of AI.

Law 5321/2026 makes it the market-surveillance authority for AI systems in the AI Act's prohibited practices, high-risk systems in Annex III and systems with transparency obligations under Article 50.

name: EETT AI Coordination and Expertise Centre
role: Law 5321/2026 tasks it with supporting the data protection authority and the market-surveillance authorities named in Article 3(2) of the law.

name: Εθνική Επιτροπή Τηλεπικοινωνιών και Ταχυδρομείων (EETT)
role: Law 5321/2026 designates it, with the data protection authority, as competent authority for operating the AI regulatory sandbox.

name: AKOS
role: ZIUDHPUI, the act implementing the AI Act, makes it responsible for setting up AI regulatory sandboxes under Article 57 of the AI Act. ZIUDHPUI makes it responsible for supervising the compliance of high-risk AI systems governed by the Union legislation in Annex I Section A of the AI Act.

name: AI Competence Centre (KCUI)
role: The government says it operates as the central national hub for AI experts, technologies, services and information.

name: Informacijski pooblaščenec (IP)
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it responsible for supervising the provisions of Article 5 of the AI Act.

name: Agencija za zavarovalni nadzor (AZN)
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it responsible for supervising high-risk AI systems in Annex III point 5(c) of the AI Act.

name: Banka Slovenije
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it responsible for supervising high-risk AI systems in Annex III point 5(b) of the AI Act when credit institutions place them on the market, put them into service or use them.

name: Tržni inšpektorat (TIRS)
name_en: Market Inspectorate of the Republic of Slovenia
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it responsible for supervising the high-risk AI systems of the preceding paragraph that are used by credit providers it supervises under the consumer-credit law.

name: Ministry responsible for the market
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it the notifying authority for high-risk AI systems in products under Annex I Section A points 1, 3 to 7, 9 and 10 of the AI Act.

name: Ministry responsible for infrastructure
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it the notifying authority for high-risk AI systems in products under Annex I Section A point 8 of the AI Act.

name: Ministry responsible for health
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it the notifying authority for high-risk AI systems in products under Annex I Section A point 2 of the AI Act.

name: Javna agencija Republike Slovenije za zdravila in medicinske pripomočke (JAZMP)
name_en: Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices of the Republic of Slovenia
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it the notifying authority for high-risk AI systems in products under Annex I Section A points 11 and 12 of the AI Act.

name: Ministry responsible for the information society
role: ZIUDHPUI makes it the notifying authority for high-risk AI systems in Annex III point 1 of the AI Act.

name: AI CyberLab
role: The ministry's project plan says research organisations develop new knowledge, models and methods, while "AI CyberLab will ensure their verification, testing and implementation support" when they are introduced into public administration information systems, from a cybersecurity perspective. The ministry's project plan says the laboratory will enable public authorities to test the security and robustness of AI solutions before they are deployed. The minutes of the Programme Slovakia monitoring committee's commission record a ministry representative saying AI CyberLab will enable verification of solutions, for example in AI, from a cybersecurity perspective and of their compliance with national and international standards.

name: Artificial Intelligence Centre (MIC)
role: The Artificial Intelligence Centre Law tasks it with organising, with the competent institutions, a special regulatory environment in which rules different from those in force may apply, so that AI systems can be developed, tested and improved. The Artificial Intelligence Centre Law tasks it with promoting the application of AI technologies in the public and private sectors.

name: Commissioner for Personal Data Protection
role: The deputy ministry says it has been designated market-surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in points 1, 6, 7 and 8 of Annex III of the AI Act.

name: National AI Taskforce
role: The Presidency says the Strategy was drawn up by the National AI Taskforce, which a Council of Ministers decision set up.

name: European AI Certification Lab
role: The draft national AI strategy lists a "European AI Certification Lab and sandbox capability enabling precertification of high-risk and foundation models in Cyprus".

name: Malta Digital Innovation Authority
role: Legal Notice 226 of 2025 makes it the national authority responsible for the establishment and functioning of a national AI regulatory sandbox.

name: Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC)
role: Legal Notice 227 of 2025 makes it the market-surveillance authority for listed high-risk AI systems, among them high-risk systems used for law enforcement in so far as their use is permitted by law.

name: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA)
role: The EU cybersecurity agency; the EU's institute record is the AI Office. A Commission spokesperson said on 11 September 2026 that, after safeguards and terms were agreed with Anthropic, the Commission had official access to its model Mythos 5 and the cybersecurity agency was testing it. The Next Web reported on 10 September that access came more than three months after Anthropic agreed in principle in June; Techzine reported the same day that the access was limited to defensive use and that the agency did not have access to Mythos 5.1.

name: China AI Safety and Development Association (CnAISDA)
role: Tsinghua describes the association's frontier AI safety evaluation research and representation of China in international dialogue. It is a research network jointly created by Chinese universities, institutes and think tanks, with reported government support. No national government designation act was identified in the reviewed sources.

name: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT)
role: It runs voluntary, opt-in AI safety benchmark evaluations with certificates through the industry alliance AIIA. It is a state research institute under the industry ministry.

name: TC260
role: It publishes the AI Safety Governance Framework. It is a national cybersecurity standards committee.

name: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)
role: It runs security filing for generative AI services. It is an internet regulator.

name: AI Product and System Evaluation Center (AIEC)
role: It evaluates language models for trustworthiness, local-language performance and Taiwan's social context and values. It is a Ministry of Digital Affairs programme. The ministry works closely with ITRI and the National Institute of Cyber Security and discussed evaluation of frontier models in 2024. Trustworthiness and performance testing do not by themselves establish the qualifying model-evaluation assignment.

name: National Institute of Cyber Security (NICS)
role: It has tested DeepSeek model safeguards and jailbreak resistance, and OpenClaw and NemoClaw agent security. It is an institute under the Ministry of Digital Affairs. These tests do not by themselves establish designation as the national advanced-AI safety institute.

name: AI Malaysia Berhad
role: Serving as the national AI Safety Institute is one of its pillars. It is a national AI entity under the Ministry of Digital.

name: AI Safety Institute Indonesia (AISII)
role: It is an initiative of KORIKA, an independent membership association (perkumpulan); no government mandate was found.

name: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
role: It leads AI policy. In May 2026 it completed inter-ministerial discussion of the draft presidential regulations on an AI roadmap and AI ethics, before their submission to the President.

name: AI Governance Practice Center (AIGPC), ETDA
role: It provides guidance, training and some language-model testing with the banking sector. It is the AI governance centre of the Electronic Transactions Development Agency. A governance sandbox is planned for 2027. The centre has no mandate to evaluate advanced models.

name: Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST)
role: It manages AI for the state under the 2025 AI Law. It runs the national AI portal for risk notifications and incident reports.

name: National AI Center for Research and Innovation (NAICRI)
role: It is an AI research and computing hub of the Department of Science and Technology, launched February 2026; it has no evaluation mandate.

name: National Digital Economy Authority (proposed)
role: Its proposed tasks include AI safety standards, risk classification and certification. The draft strategy proposes it as a regulator.

name: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam (AITI)
role: It issued the AI governance and ethics guide with an AI Governance and Ethics Working Group. It is an ICT sector authority.

name: Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC)
role: It leads the drafting of the National AI Strategy with UN-ESCAP support.

name: Ministry of Technology and Communications
role: It leads the draft National AI Strategy and the UNESCO AI readiness assessment.

name: National Institute of Metrology of Myanmar
role: It signed an agreement on AI-powered metrology cooperation in August 2025; this does not establish a mandate to evaluate advanced AI models.

name: Ministry of Science and Technology
role: It led National AI Strategy and National AI Policy drafting reported in 2025; the retrieved announcements do not propose a named AI safety institute.

name: National Artificial Intelligence Development Department
role: It is reported as established under the Ministry of Digital Development and Communications by July 2026 to accelerate AI technology development; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was found.

name: Ministry of Transport and Communications
role: It is a partner in the UNESCO AI readiness assessment. This was reported by Catalpa International.

name: TIC Timor
role: It is a partner in the readiness assessment. It is a government ICT agency.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Digital FSM project
role: It is a government programme for digital connectivity, government services and enabling legal and regulatory arrangements; no advanced AI model-evaluation mandate was identified.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Ministry of Information, Communication, Transport and Tourism Development
role: It issued the 2019 National ICT Policy, covering digital services, connectivity and cyber safeguards; no qualifying model-evaluation designation was found.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Digital RMI project
role: It is a government programme for telecommunications reform, digital government, cybersecurity and digital skills; no qualifying AI institute was identified.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Department of ICT
role: It has a central technical and implementation role in the 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy, including digital government services and cybersecurity; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Standing Committee on Cybersecurity, Telecommunications and Technology, Olbiil Era Kelulau
role: It is a parliamentary committee assigned the cybersecurity legislation; no national mandate for an institute to evaluate advanced models was identified.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body. This was reported by Pacific Islands News Association (PINA).

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body. This was reported by Pacific Islands News Association (PINA).

name: Tuvalu Computer Emergency Response Team (proposed in the 2021 ICT policy)
role: The 2021 policy proposes a cyber task force.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Office of the Government Chief Information Officer / Department of Communication and Digital Transformation
role: It is a government digital agency that led the Digital Transformation Masterplan; no AI evaluation role was found.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body.

name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body. This was reported by Pacific Islands News Association (PINA).

name: Secretariat of State for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications
role: It leads the ethical AI and business-adoption measures described in the government announcements; no designation for evaluation of the safety of advanced models was identified.

name: AKSHI AI Directorate
role: It works on public-sector AI and EU alignment. It is part of the National Agency for Information Society. No model-evaluation mandate was stated.

name: Virtual Institute of AI
role: It links researchers and start-ups to mentoring, funding and cloud support as a Ministry of High-Tech Industry platform. No model-evaluation mandate was described.

name: State Service for Special Communications and Information Security
role: It is tasked by the AI strategy with analysing information-security risks of AI in state bodies; this is not model evaluation.

name: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina AI institute envisaged in the 2021-2027 development strategy
role: Measure 1.1.4 envisages a federally funded institute researching AI applications with academic, business and public-sector partners; no mandate to evaluate advanced models for their capabilities or behaviour risks was identified.

name: Blum research institute for computer science and engineering, artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems
role: The 2024 Sarajevo Canton feasibility-study announcement describes applied AI research in health, energy, education and manufacturing. This subnational proposal does not identify a national mandate to evaluate the safety of advanced models.

name: Planned national AI centre
role: It is planned as a laboratory and technology hub, announced in February 2026 by the First Deputy Minister of Digital Development; no model-evaluation mandate was described.

name: Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Management, Ministry of AI and Digital Development
role: It is responsible for AI regulation, data and coordination of the National AI Platform. It is a ministry unit. The ministry's October 2026 briefing separates rule-making from audits conducted by independent specialists and organisations.

name: Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute (kaisi.kz)
role: Its archived site describes research on capabilities, risks and mitigations concerning advanced models. It is a research organisation using the Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute name.

name: Direction des Plateformes et des Ressources Numériques, Data Programme
role: It has responsibilities for data and AI deployment, including public-service applications. It is a government unit. No national mandate to evaluate advanced models for their capabilities or behaviour risks was identified in its official job specification.

name: Sub-Council for Artificial Intelligence and Applied Research (SCIA)
role: It helps prepare strategy and AI Act transposition as a consultative body of two ministries. It has no evaluation mandate.

name: Ministry of Digital Development: draft model-check scheme
role: According to a single press source, the draft provides for accredited-lab checks of models seeking national or sovereign status under Law 243-FZ, for legal and values compliance, and by-laws were still in inter-agency agreement as of August 2026.

name: San Marino Innovation (Istituto per l'Innovazione della Repubblica di San Marino)
role: It supports start-up development, training and digital policy as a national innovation institute. Its published cooperation with Olitec discusses cybersecurity and emerging-technology risks without a designated mandate to evaluate advanced models.

name: Institute of Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence, International University of Tourism and Entrepreneurship of Tajikistan
role: It was established by government resolution on 10 March 2026 as a university educational institution for specialist training; no national mandate to evaluate the safety of advanced models was identified.

name: Regional Artificial Intelligence Centre, IT Hub Dushanbe (planned)
role: The June 2026 official announcement describes research laboratories, specialist training, model training and data infrastructure; no mandate to evaluate advanced models for their capabilities or behaviour risks was identified.

name: Agency of Innovation and Digital Technologies under the President of Tajikistan
role: The amended AI strategy identifies the agency as the public authority for digital technologies and the digital economy; general coordination and regulatory functions do not establish an AISI.

name: AI Development/Competence Centre at TurkmenTelecom (planned)
role: Ministerial announcements describe an AI centre for national digital priorities, applied research and specialist training, including sectoral pilot projects. No remit to evaluate advanced models for their capabilities or behaviour risks was identified.

name: Ministry of Communications
role: UNDP describes the Ministry of Communications as leading national AI strategy work with UNDP; a general strategy-development process does not itself establish an AI safety institute or a study of that option.

name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Artificial Intelligence Institute
role: Its tests cover security, performance, robustness, bias, explainability, data protection and cyber resistance. Pre-deployment and major-update testing applies to high-impact systems defined by sensitive uses. It is an existing public AI institute whose general AI safety-assessment capacity is strengthened by action 16. A national general-purpose/frontier capability or behaviour-risk evaluation remit remains unresolved.

name: Cybersecurity Presidency (Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı)
role: It coordinates technical safety assessment alongside existing public bodies; participation in the action plan is not designation of an AISI.

name: National AI Ethics Board (planned in action 4)
role: It would provide guidance, ethical assessment and referral of submissions. Binding supervision would remain with sectoral regulators. No designation to evaluate advanced models was found.

name: Planned Digital Regulator (draft AI law)
role: It would write by-laws and guidance, with checks and post-market monitoring of general-purpose models; the draft law is not yet adopted.

name: Centre for the Development of AI and the Digital Economy
role: It runs the national AI portal and monitors AI projects. It is a state body under the Ministry of Digital Technologies. It is not a model-evaluation institute.

name: Ministry of Information and Communications Technology
role: It led the UNESCO AI readiness assessment pilot reported in August 2024; no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: AGETIC
role: It is reported as regulator or strategy author under the Senate bill. It is a digital government agency. No model evaluation mandate was found.

name: Autoridad de Regulacion de la Inteligencia Artificial (ARIA, proposed)
role: It is a regulator with sanctioning powers in the Senate bill as reported; it is not an evaluation institute.

name: Centro Nacional de Transparência Algorítmica e IA Confiável (PBIA action 51)
role: Its remit covers research and studies on AI risks, safety, transparency and reliability, supporting systems auditing and evaluation. It is a national research centre provided for in PBIA action 51, with R$ 40 million for 2024-2028. Whether this covers evaluation of advanced models remains unresolved. The August UFMG implementation report still requires accessible primary confirmation.

name: Brazilian Institute for AI Safety and Opportunities (AISO), non-governmental proposal
role: CEBRI and ITS Rio published an institutional design on 18 September 2025. The full report describes an exploratory proposal to stimulate debate. No government appointment as an inquiry, formal government proposal or adoption was found.

name: ANPD and the regulatory system discussed under PL 2338/2023
role: ANPD handles data protection, and AI regulation is proposed. PL 2338/2023 awaits a rapporteur opinion. The government bill PL 6237/2025 joined to it proposes regulatory coordination and advisory committees. ANPD finished the tests of its first AI and data-protection sandbox, publishing the final monitoring report on 5 November 2026, and is preparing a second edition on the safe use of digital games by children and adolescents. No designation as a national institute to evaluate advanced models was established.

name: Ministry of Innovation and National Development
role: It announced planned AI legislation and governance structures in June 2026; no evaluation body was described.

name: National AI Commission
role: It is proposed in the Speech from the Throne of 20 May 2026, to be established under a planned Artificial Intelligence Governance Act; no evaluation or testing remit was described.

name: Ministry of Economic Transformation
role: It announced the intention to develop a national AI policy; it has no evaluation mandate.

name: Consejo Asesor Técnico de IA (proposed, Ministry of Science)
role: It would propose lists of high-risk systems and review the law. It would be an advisory body under the Senate bill, with no model evaluation mandate.

name: Agencia de Protección de Datos Personales
role: It would hold inspection and sanction powers under the bill; it would be a regulator, not an evaluation institute.

name: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación
role: It would be the national AI authority under the bill, with a policy and regulatory role; it would not be a model evaluation institute.

name: MICITT
role: It leads the AI strategy and would be the supervisory authority in bill 23.771. It is the science and technology ministry. It is not an evaluation institute.

name: Ministry of Communications (MINCOM)
role: It leads the national AI strategy and its advisory council; it provides general risk and impact oversight, and no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: Caribbean Digital Transformation Project, Dominica
role: It is a government digital infrastructure, skills and service modernisation project; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was found.

name: Government of Dominica / UNDP Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (reported)
role: Q95FM reports a 12 October 2026 readiness-assessment launch covering the AI ecosystem, government use, regulation and ethics. This concerns general AI readiness; it is not a verified government study of establishing an AISI.

name: OGTIC and Gabinete de Innovacion y Desarrollo Digital
role: They lead the national AI strategy; they have no model evaluation mandate.

name: Comite Nacional de sandboxes regulatorios de IA (planned in ENIA)
role: It would assess regulatory sandboxes and regulatory options; it is not a model evaluation institute.

name: Comision Presidencial de Gobierno Abierto y Electronico (GAE)
role: GAE's own account describes a multisector AI-policy dialogue with UNDP support and UNDP's presentation of the AI Landscape Assessment; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified in the retrieved material.

name: SENACYT
role: It leads AI strategy work as a science and technology secretariat. No evaluation mandate was found.

name: Banque de la Republique d'Haiti and Ministere de l'Economie et des Finances
role: They co-organised the June 2025 Ayiti AI Summit. No regulatory or evaluation mandate was found.

name: National AI Task Force (Office of the Prime Minister)
role: It is drafting the national AI policy and a legislative framework; it is advisory, with no model evaluation mandate.

name: Ministry of Education and Digital Transformation
role: An education-sector AI framework is in preparation. In January 2026, the minister said that AI policy discussions were ongoing and should reach Cabinet. In October 2026, the minister spoke on limiting AI dependence in schools. No evaluation mandate was found.

name: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT)
role: The agency's substantive AI page describes training, public-service AI applications and national supercomputing plans. The reviewed page does not establish a national institute to evaluate advanced models. The saved rendered copy was reread; fresh access failed.

name: Consejo Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial and Plataforma Nacional de Auditoría Algorítmica (PNAA)
role: PNAA would evaluate data, models and systems for equity, explainability, traceability and rights protection as a technical body under the National AI Council. Both bodies are proposed in the bill presented on 30 April 2025. The bill also permits tools for detecting systemic risks. The reviewed provisions do not establish a remit to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks. The retrieved official legislative record lists the bill as pending in committee.

name: Comision Nacional para Tecnologias Criticas y Emergentes
role: It was set up to manage technology risks and oversee the AI and semiconductor strategies. It is a cross-government commission established by Executive Decree 36 (2026). No model evaluation mandate was reported.

name: SENACYT
role: It gives technical support to the AI strategy as a science secretariat. No evaluation mandate was found.

name: Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INC, planned)
role: The adopted strategy plans a national cybersecurity institute with an AI-security specialisation, including monitoring adversarial attacks on national AI models. No remit to evaluate advanced models is stated. The national red team is assigned to the government, not directly to INC.

name: Observatorio de Riesgos de IA (SENACYT, planned)
role: It would monitor global AI safety trends and track local algorithmic harm incidents, with annual reports for lawmakers and regulators; the plan concerns incident and trend monitoring rather than model evaluation.

name: Instituto Nacional de IA Aplicada (INIAA, planned)
role: It is planned as 'not a regulator but an execution engine' for adoption and delivery; it has no evaluation mandate.

name: Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital (PCM)
role: It leads AI policy, the national strategy and the state AI catalogue; no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: MITIC
role: It leads national AI policy and the UNESCO readiness assessment; no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation (EZOTI)
role: EZOTI's official report announced the forthcoming UNESCO AI readiness assessment; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified.

name: Agencia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (ANIA)
role: It promotes AI and provides light-touch supervision through a registry, standards, a sandbox, and voluntary and mandatory registration; no mandate for it to evaluate advanced models was identified, so it is not counted.

name: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence (MPAAI)
role: It leads national AI policy work and the UNESCO readiness assessment; no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: AI Innovation Centre (UWI St Augustine)
role: It is a university research and governance centre; it is not a government-designated evaluation body.

name: AGESIC
role: As of June 2026, it was studying an AI profile for the cybersecurity framework and had not updated its guidance. It is a digital government agency. It is not an evaluation institute.

name: Instituto Vidart (Centro Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial)
role: Its research lines include safety and explainability. It is a national AI research centre launched on 7 September 2026 by Uruguay Innova, SENCI and AGESIC. It has no evaluation or audit mandate.

name: Ministry of Science and Technology (MINCYT)
role: It leads the national AI programme as the science ministry. Its May 2026 account describes a prospective national AI institute addressing bias and local data infrastructure. The account does not establish a qualifying remit to evaluate advanced models.

name: Agencia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (proposed in the AI bill)
role: The 13 November 2024 draft reproduced on an unofficial legal website proposes a public institute under the science ministry with standards, registries, supervision and sanctions. Article 12.16 includes model-risk assessment for exceptional authorisations of otherwise unacceptable AI uses; a remit to test advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks remains unconfirmed.

name: National AI Test and Validation Lab
role: It is a certification lab for AI models, agents and apps, governed by the UAE Cyber Security Council and operated with Cisco and Open Innovation AI (May 2026).

name: Cyber Security Council
role: It governs the test lab. It is a federal cyber security body.

name: Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data
role: Policy, legislation, standards and compliance are its announced responsibilities. The June 2026 announcement says it brings together the functions previously held by the AI office, the digital government sector of the telecommunications regulator and the UAE Data Office; no testing mandate was found.

name: SDAIA
role: It published a National AI Risk Management Framework in April 2026 that sets no model-testing rules. It is a national data and AI authority.

name: National AI Directorate
role: It coordinates the national AI programme, including compute, research, skills and applications, as a Prime Minister's Office body. Its programme page does not identify a qualifying institute to evaluate the safety of advanced models.

name: National Institute for Impact Driven AI
role: It is described in the National AI Directorate's programme as applying AI to medicine, genomics, climate and infrastructure. No explicit mandate to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks was identified.

name: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
role: It leads the national AI strategy, including its ethics and governance area.

name: المركز الوطني للذكاء الاصطناعي
role: Its remit covers the national AI strategy, AI regulatory frameworks and policies, platforms, research and adoption support. It was set up in 2026 as a communications ministry unit attached to the minister. The decision does not assign model evaluation or testing.

name: AI Safety and Security Centre in Higher Education
role: Its proposed remit covers research, training and a register of high-risk AI in the sector. The Academy of Scientific Research and Technology called for proposals for the centre in March 2025.

name: National Council for AI
role: It oversees the national AI strategy 2025-2030.

name: Jazari Institutes
role: They form a national network of AI centres for training, research and incubation.

name: AI Council
role: It oversees the National AI Policy 2025 as a ministerial council.

name: Independent Oversight Committee (proposed)
role: It would audit AI systems for bias under the draft policy; it is not an evaluation institute.

name: Information & eGovernment Authority
role: It leads digital government and AI readiness work.

name: National AI Organisation
role: It is an AI strategy and development body under the President, approved by parliament in October 2025.

name: GovTech Agency
role: It drafted the National AI Strategy 2025 and leads digital policy.

name: National AI governing body (proposed)
role: The strategy lists the proposed governing body as an action under its governance enabler. No mandate to evaluate models was stated.

name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation
role: With UN ESCWA it organised a consultation workshop on the draft national AI strategy, as reported by UN ESCWA.

name: National Scientific Council on AI
role: It assesses resources and proposes training plans and international cooperation. It is an advisory body under the higher education and knowledge economy ministers.

name: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
role: It chairs the strategy's implementation coordination meetings.

name: Communications and Media Commission
role: The CMC consultation draft's contents list licensing requirements and risk classification; Iraq Business News dates the consultation to 23 September 2026. The draft is not evidence of enacted rules or an institute to evaluate advanced models.

name: National Centre for Artificial Intelligence
role: It is attached to the Prime Minister's Office; no evaluation or testing role was described in the sources read.

name: Central Agency for Information Technology (CAIT)
role: It leads government digital transformation and partnered with UNDP on the AI Landscape Assessment (September 2026).

name: Ministry of State for Technology and Artificial Intelligence (MITAI/OMSITAI)
role: It leads the national digital transformation and AI strategy; its earlier five-year LEAP plan covers 2025-2030.

name: Lebanese Digital and AI Agency (LEDAIA, proposed)
role: It is proposed in the 2032 strategy as its 'executive engine', carrying delivery and technical oversight.

name: Lebanon AI Evaluation Office (proposed)
role: It is proposed in the ministry's 2032 draft strategy to independently assess whether AI systems are fit for sensitive-domain deployment, reporting to the AI National Council. This deployment-assurance role does not by itself establish evaluation of advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

name: Cybersecurity Institute with an AI Security and Red-Team Lab (proposed)
role: The ministry's draft strategy lists an AI Security and Red-Team Lab within the Cybersecurity Institute's cybersecurity and digital-trust programme. The lab's technical remit is not specified; a qualifying mandate to evaluate advanced models remains unresolved.

name: AI National Council (proposed)
role: It would sign off a quarterly scoreboard as an oversight body comprising private sector, diaspora, university and civil society members.

name: General Information Authority
role: It led the drafting of the AI Ethics Charter and, with ESCWA, the strategy.

name: National oversight body for AI ethics (proposed)
role: It is proposed in the charter under the Council of Ministers to supervise compliance and approve high-risk systems; pre-deployment assessment stays with the deploying institution. This was reported by SMEX.

name: Maldives Digital Service
role: It was established on 15 January 2026, when the National Centre for Information Technology (NCIT) was abolished, and was to assume all of NCIT's responsibilities; NCIT had worked with the steering committee that compiled the UNESCO readiness assessment launched on 31 July 2025.

name: Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology
role: It is responsible, with the economic development ministry, for presenting the masterplan to Cabinet.

name: AI Regulation Council
role: Its Nepali compliance clause requires adherence to approved AI policies, laws and standards. The English version also says to test compliance. It is a minister-chaired Council under policy section 10.1. The Rising Nepal reported on 10 November 2025 that the minister said the Council had formed. No constituting decision was retrieved.

name: National AI Centre
role: Policy section 10.2 assigns it programme evaluation, product and service standards, risk mitigation and the Council secretariat. It is a centre under the communications ministry, reported by The Rising Nepal as inaugurated on 10 November 2025. These tasks do not establish evaluation of advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

name: AI Excellence Centres
role: They are planned in universities and research institutions for AI research and training.

name: Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology
role: It issued the AI policy (Circular 11/2025, 9 April 2025); it monitors compliance by government units and reports to the Council of Ministers.

name: Sector regulators
role: They monitor compliance with the policy by the institutions in the sectors they supervise.

name: AI Experts Committee
role: It advises decision-makers on AI opportunities and challenges. It is an advisory committee formed by the transport and communications ministry under Ministerial Decision 124/2025, with a three-year term. No testing role was described.

name: Ministry of Communications and Technology
role: It co-sponsors AI training initiatives and the first national AI conference (June 2026); no safety or evaluation mandate was described.

name: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS)
role: It leads AI policy and the UNESCO readiness assessment through its National Directorate for Cybersecurity Policies and Digital Services. Its September 2025 draft AI law is published for consultation.

name: Agência de Proteção de Dados
role: It is a data protection authority; it has no AI evaluation mandate.

name: Autoridade Competente da IA (proposed)
role: It would organise AI product and service risk assessments and supervise compliance. Articles 61-62 of the ministry's draft AI law envisage it as a regulator to be established by separate regulation. General-purpose AI developers would separately conduct and report evaluations under article 56. Articles 58(2)(e) and 63(2) also envisage AI evaluation services and mechanisms. Their remit covering advanced models remains unresolved.

name: Ministry of Digital Transition
role: It coordinates AI policy in practice; it is not an evaluation body. This was reported by Droit Médias Finance.

name: Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés
role: It is a data protection authority; it has no AI mandate.

name: Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy
role: It leads the AI strategy with UNDP support; it owns the policy.

name: Commission Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle (planned)
role: It is a governance body provided for in the validated strategy; no evaluation mandate was reported. This was reported by Digital Business Africa.

name: Agence des Systèmes d'Information et du Numérique (ASIN)
role: It contributes to implementing AI projects under the strategy; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles (APDP)
role: It protects personal data and privacy as an independent authority. No national mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified in the retrieved mission statement.

name: Ministry of Communications and Innovation
role: Its assistant minister said in August 2025 that the government is working on finalising a national AI policy.

name: Information and Data Protection Commission
role: It is a data regulator; it has no AI mandate. This was reported by Lawyers Hub, Africa AI Policy Lab.

name: Ministry of the Digital Economy
role: It leads the draft national AI strategy and digital plan 2026-2030; it owns the policy.

name: Congolese Academy of Artificial Intelligence (planned)
role: It is a planned training, innovation and applied-research academy announced by the Ministry of Digital Economy; no designation to evaluate advanced models was identified in the announcement.

name: ARCEP Centrafrique
role: It regulates electronic communications and postal services; no advanced AI model-evaluation mandate was identified in its published missions.

name: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy
role: It owns digital and AI policy.

name: ARPCE
role: It convened a January 2026 seminar on digital regulation, including AI. It is a telecommunications regulator. No mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified.

name: African Research Centre for Artificial Intelligence (CARIA)
role: Created by Law 14-2024 as a public research, training and development establishment, under the digital economy minister's administrative and technical supervision and the scientific research minister's scientific supervision; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MINPOSTEL)
role: It is responsible for CONIA consultations and development of a national AI strategy. Its 2024 account records a recommendation for a strategy roadmap, not a model-evaluation institute.

name: AI authority and Presidential AI Council (proposed)
role: They are proposed in the strategy according to the secondary profile. They had not been gazetted as of June 2026.

name: Digital and AI Centre of Excellence (planned)
role: It is a planned skills and talent centre; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Núcleo Nacional de Cibersegurança
role: It is a cybersecurity unit; it has no AI evaluation mandate.

name: Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute (EAII)
role: Its remit covers research, development and policy implementation. The national policy also assigns developer licensing and certification of domestic and imported AI products and services. It is an autonomous federal AI institute accountable to the Prime Minister under regulation 510/2022. No qualifying role in evaluating the safety of advanced models was identified.

name: Ministry of the Digital Economy, Digitalisation and Innovation
role: It runs the strategy consultations with UNDP; it owns the policy. This was reported by Osiris.

name: National Technical Committee on AI (CTN-IA)
role: It is a coordination body; no evaluation mandate was reported.

name: ANSSI
role: It is a national cybersecurity agency; it has no AI evaluation mandate.

name: Information Commission
role: It oversees data protection; the retained secondary profile identifies no explicit AI evaluation mandate.

name: National Misinformation and Disinformation Response Centre
role: It was launched under the Ministry of Information in April 2026 to detect, verify and respond to false information; no advanced AI model-evaluation designation was found.

name: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy
role: It validated the national AI roadmap with UNDP; it owns the policy. This was reported by Ecofin Agency.

name: National AI Governance Council (proposed)
role: It is proposed per the secondary profile; it is not established.

name: Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation
role: It includes a Secretary of State responsible for AI Systems, according to the government's June 2026 account; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified.

name: ARCGEM
role: It is a telecom regulator; it has no AI mandate.

name: Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
role: It proposed the national digital transformation strategy approved by decree 10/2025. No designation to evaluate advanced models was identified in the retrieved governance evidence.

name: Instituto Tecnológico para a Modernização Administrativa (ITMA)
role: It handles administrative modernisation and public digital services; the strategy envisages a cybersecurity unit, without assigning advanced AI model evaluation.

name: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy (MICDE)
role: It leads the AI strategy and the draft AI policy; it owns the policy and is not an evaluation body.

name: Special Envoy for Technology (Amb. Philip Thigo)
role: The Special Envoy represented Kenya at the November 2024 launch of the international network of AI safety institutes.

name: Commission for the assessment of AI readiness
role: It was reported by the Council of Ministers in March 2026 as assessing national institutional, technical and regulatory capacity; no advanced AI model-evaluation mandate or AISI study was identified.

name: Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications
role: It runs the 'Digital Liberia' strategic plan; it owns the policy.

name: Office of Technology, Digitization and Innovation (OTDI)
role: It was created by Executive Order 163 of April 2026 to coordinate digital transformation; it has no AI evaluation mandate.

name: Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation (MICSTI)
role: It leads the AI policy and the strategy drafting; it owns the policy and is not an evaluation body.

name: Ministry of Digital Development, Posts and Telecommunications
role: It owns digital policy and signed the 2024 feasibility agreement for an applied-AI institute.

name: Centre d'intelligence artificielle et de robotique du Mali (CIAR-Mali)
role: It is a public scientific and technological institution for training, research and AI/robotics solutions; no evaluation mandate was described.

name: Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Modernization of Administration
role: It authored the draft strategy and owns the policy; it is not an evaluation body.

name: AI Unit, Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation
role: It leads the national AI strategy; it is a policy unit, and no model evaluation mandate was found.

name: Department of e-Government
role: It leads the national AI strategy drafting with UNDP; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Centro Nacional de Testes, Avaliação e Auditoria de IA / Sandbox Regulatório Nacional de IA (draft P6.I5)
role: It is a proposed testing, model evaluation, certification and audit centre combined with a regulatory sandbox. Draft 6 covers imported, open, proprietary, adapted and domestic models and testing before public or institutional adoption. INTIC, the CNIA executive secretariat and sectoral regulators are assigned implementation. The stated remit is assurance before adoption; the text does not specify the qualifying model class and capability or behaviour-risk function.

name: Comissão Nacional de Inteligência Artificial (CNIA)
role: It advises on AI policies, research institutions and adoption. It is a consultative and technical advisory body subordinate to the Council of Ministers. Decree 14/2026 created it, taking effect on publication on 17 April 2026. The retrieved decree does not assign a unit to evaluate advanced models.

name: National Artificial Intelligence Institute
role: The ministry describes developing and testing local AI solutions. The institute was officially launched on 23 September 2026 and anchored at NCRST. It has centres for research and development, datasets, software development and AI innovation. The retrieved announcements do not establish a mandate to evaluate the safety of advanced models.

name: National Commission on Research, Science and Technology (NCRST)
role: It is reported to be developing the national AI strategy.

name: National Cybersecurity Centre (CNAC)
role: Its intended role is to coordinate information-systems and critical-infrastructure security. The Council of Ministers approved its creation and statutes in October 2025. No advanced AI model-evaluation mandate was found.

name: Ministry of Communication and New Information Technologies
role: It announced the intention to develop an AI and data strategy in July 2025; the announcement names no safety or model-evaluation institute.

name: National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR), NITDA
role: It is a NITDA research and innovation centre for AI and other emerging technologies; no advanced-AI-model evaluation mandate was identified.

name: National Artificial Intelligence Agency (approved June 2026)
role: It is a general AI development and governance agency; no model evaluation mandate was found in the report read.

name: Responsible AI Office, MINICT
role: It is called for in the 2023 National AI Policy to coordinate implementation; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development
role: It authored the AI in Education Framework 2026-2030, a sector policy framework; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Department of Information Communications Technology (DICT)
role: It handles government ICT policy and infrastructure; no AI evaluation mandate was found.

name: Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority
role: The National Information Centre's government account says a prime-ministerial decision dated 5 November 2025 created the authority under the digital ministry as an evolution of the centre, covering national data management, governance and AI use for decision support and public services. The detailed statute and a qualifying remit to evaluate advanced models remain unverified.

name: Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation (MoCTI)
role: It leads the readiness assessment and the planned AI strategy; it is not an evaluation body.

name: Somalia National AI Center (SNAIC)
role: It is Somali National University's centre for AI research, education, innovation and policy. No designation to evaluate advanced models was identified in its published mission.

name: Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services
role: Officials have spoken about AI; no policy or evaluation body was found.

name: Institute for Innovation and Knowledge (INIC)
role: It can issue digital strategies and guidelines; it has limited capacity and no AI evaluation mandate.

name: National Agency for Personal Data Protection (ANPDP)
role: It is a data protection authority; it is named by UNESCO as a base for future AI governance.

name: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology
role: It is drafting the national AI strategy; it owns the policy.

name: Direction générale de l'Intelligence Artificielle
role: It was created in the Ministry of Telecommunications, Digital Economy and Digitalisation by presidential decree 2690/PR/PM/MTENDA/2025 of 21 October 2025. Its duties were not published or detailed, and no evaluation role was shown.

name: Ministry of Telecommunications, Digital Economy and Digitalisation
role: It leads the AI strategy with UN Economic Commission for Africa support.

name: Ministry of Public Service Efficiency and Digital Transformation
role: It leads digital transformation and AI-strategy work; no qualifying model-evaluation institute was identified.

name: Togo AI Lab
role: It applies data science to public policies, including health, agriculture and education, through a government and UC Berkeley CEGA partnership. No national designation to evaluate the safety of advanced models was identified.

name: National AI Council (proposed)
role: It would advise the Ministry of Technology and Science as an expert group. It is not an evaluation body.

name: Ministry of Technology and Science
role: It owns the national AI strategy.

name: Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services
role: It owns the national AI strategy and policy; it is not an evaluation body.

name: National Digital Regulatory Committee (under POTRAZ)
role: The 2025 report describes a planned committee to oversee rollout of the national AI strategy; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified in the sources reviewed.

name: AI Strategy Implementation Office (Ministry of ICT)
role: It is a planned office to oversee the rollout of the national AI strategy; establishment was not verified.
